reasons: Only the first six sections are visible, so the page body that loads and displays the report cannot be checked.
No test or error handling for a failed report load is visible.
The confidence score can be null, and how the page handles that is not visible.

terms.meaning: a library for building web pages out of reusable parts
a helper library that fetches data from the server and keeps it up to date on the page
a written description of the shape of some data, so the code knows which fields to expect
the agreed list of industry and sub-industry categories that projects should fit into
an empty value, meaning no data was recorded

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and building blocks
sections.what: Brings in the tools the page needs: data loading, page links, a card layout, the industry lookup and context, the state helper, and the icons. These let the page load data, navigate, and draw its layout.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs these pieces before any of its own code can run.
sections.watch_out: The industry lookup is imported from a shared folder through an alias path, so moving that folder would break this page.

sections.name: FieldCompleteness
sections.title: Field completeness row shape
sections.what: Describes one row of the completeness table: the field name, how many projects have it filled, the total project count, and the percentage. The page uses these rows to show how complete each field is.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape lets the page show each field the same way.
sections.watch_out: The percentage is taken as given from the server, and this file does not check that it matches the counts.

sections.name: DriftRow
sections.title: Taxonomy problem row shape
sections.what: Describes one project flagged for a taxonomy problem: its ID, name, industry, optional sub-industry, and a reason. The reason is either that the sub-industry is not in the list or that it is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reason is limited to two values so the page can explain each problem the same way.
sections.watch_out: The two reason values must match exactly what the server sends, or the page may show a wrong or blank explanation.

sections.name: QualityReport
sections.title: Full quality report shape
sections.what: Describes the whole report: when it was made, the total project count, the number of projects per industry, the completeness rows, the taxonomy problems, projects missing evidence, and projects with low confidence scores.
sections.why: Likely reason: one description of the whole report keeps the page and the server agreeing on the data.
sections.watch_out: The confidence score can be empty for a project, so anything that displays it must handle that case.

sections.name: FIELD_LABELS, NA
sections.title: Readable field names and N/A marker
sections.what: Maps internal field names such as capacity value and planned budget to readable labels, and defines a grey N/A marker shown when a value is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner reads these labels, not internal field names, so the mapping keeps the page readable.
sections.watch_out: A field missing from this list is likely to appear under its raw internal name.

sections.name: industryName
sections.title: Industry display name lookup
sections.what: Turns an industry code into its display name from the shared list. If the code is unknown, it returns the code itself.
sections.why: Likely reason: falling back to the code keeps the page showing something even when an industry is not in the list.
sections.watch_out: An unknown or misspelled industry code appears as raw text, which can hide a data error.

sections.name: DataQuality (part 1)
sections.title: Page setup, scope and loading messages
sections.what: Starts the Data Quality Control Center page. It asks the server for the quality report, limited to the current industry when one is set. While loading it shows a progress message, and if the request fails it shows the error. It also draws the header with a back link and a Refresh button.
sections.why: The code comment says the old admin route has no industry and shows all industries, while industry-specific routes show only one industry.
sections.watch_out: The Refresh button is disabled while a fetch is running, so a slow request blocks repeated clicks until it finishes.

sections.name: DataQuality (part 2)
sections.title: Totals and projects-by-industry chips
sections.what: Shows the total number of projects and the time the report was built. Next to it, it lists each industry with its project count, largest first.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The generated time is when the report was built, not the current state of the data. The number shown in the header counts industries, not projects.

sections.name: DataQuality (part 3)
sections.title: Field completeness bars and drift card
sections.what: For each key field, shows how many projects have a value and as a percentage, with a bar. Bars under 50 percent turn amber. The taxonomy drift card starts here and turns red when any drift is found. Drift means a project's industry or sub-industry is missing or does not match the agreed list.
sections.why: Likely reason: highlights gaps and mislabeled categories so the owner can fix them.
sections.watch_out: The 50 percent amber threshold is fixed in the code, so changing what counts as a warning means editing this file.

sections.name: DataQuality (part 4)
sections.title: Drift table and missing evidence list
sections.what: Lists each drifting project with its name link, industry, sub-industry and reason. A reason of missing shows a red label, and anything else shows as not in the taxonomy. The missing evidence card has a count and a toggle. When opened, it lists projects with no active evidence quote.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the owner which records need a category fix or a source before the data can be trusted.
sections.watch_out: Any reason other than missing is labeled as not in the taxonomy, so a new reason type would show with the wrong label.

sections.name: DataQuality (part 5)
sections.title: Low confidence list and page end
sections.what: Shows a collapsible card that lists projects with a confidence score below 40, with each score next to its name. It closes the layout for the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: flags projects whose data is weakly supported so they can be reviewed first.
sections.watch_out: The title says less than 40, but the real cutoff is decided by the server, not this file. Changing one does not change the other.

summary: Data quality page: it loads a report on how complete and consistent project records are, with counts by industry, field completeness, flagged taxonomy problems, projects missing evidence, and projects with low confidence. Only the top part of the file is visible in this packet.
purpose: Likely purpose: lets the owner see where project data is missing, inconsistent, or uncertain, so they know what to fix first.
why: Likely reason: the shapes of the report are written out as types so the display code knows exactly what fields to expect from the server.
how: Step 1: the imports bring in data loading, page links, a card layout, industry lookup, the current industry context, and icons. Step 2: the shape of a completeness row, a taxonomy problem row, and the full report is described. Step 3: a label table turns internal field names into readable names, and a grey N/A marker is defined. Step 4: a helper turns an industry code into its display name. Steps 5 and later, which load the report and draw the page, are not visible in this packet, so the exact order is unclear.
inputs: A quality report from the server, requested through react-query. The current industry from the industry context. Industry codes from the shared industries list.
outputs: A rendered data quality page. The exact content of the page body is not visible in this packet.
risks: Some values can be null, such as the confidence score, and the page must handle that without breaking. The taxonomy reason text must match what the server sends. Unknown field or industry names fall back to raw text.
debug: Open the browser network tab and check the request that loads the report, then confirm its fields match the types here. If a field name shows raw instead of a label, add it to the label table. If an industry shows its raw code, check the shared industries list. If the taxonomy reasons look wrong, compare the reason text with what the server sends.
